items.title: Charlie Bocage Interview, 1960-07-18
items.q: I think we was the first colored orchestra to play appointment and engagement at the Roseland. Fifty Fweys and Broadway.

ctx.x: He told me he didn't use a mute on that.

The system of recording was different than now, you know. You had to, the soloist had to get up and walk up to there. There was big microphones sticking out. You had to get so many feet from it. You know, sometimes it would be too much and sometimes it wasn't enough. And that's kind of difficult, you know. I think we was the first colored orchestra to play appointment and engagement at the Roseland. Fifty Fweys and Broadway. That was one of the most beautiful dance palettes in America at that time. And, uh...
Did you ever have a tryout for the George White Scandals show? Well, no, uh...
